Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the demo was helpful. Before we move to a formal PO, procurement has a couple of technical questions about how you meter and round for our use case. We ingest long clinical transcripts (avg 18k tokens per session) and sometimes run multiple chained calls per patient. Specifically: 

1) Do you meter per request or per conversation window when there are multiple related calls within a 30-minute window?
2) If a single request is 18k tokens and our committed SKU is per-4k token block, how does rounding work? Do you round up to the nearest 4k for each request?
3) Are there minimum per-call charges or daily session minimums that could penalize branching workflows?

We need clarity to model costs for the board. If you can share an example invoice-friendly calculation for one patient (3 chained calls: 18k, 2k, 12k tokens) that would be great.

Also looping in Sanjay from procurement for any PO/term questions.

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a short worked example below. Looping in Vanessa (sales lead) and Marissa (billing/product) for visibility.

Short answers:
- Metering scope: we meter per "conversation window" by default for chat-style sessions (sliding 30-minute window), but per-request metering is used for single-call APIs. You can choose which behavior maps to your SKU; we'll recommend conversation-window for your workflow to avoid double-charging short chains.
- Rounding: we charge in 4k token increments for the contracted SKU. Rounding is applied per metered unit (so if you pick conversation-window, we sum tokens across related calls inside the window, then round once to the nearest 4k and bill).
- Minimums: committed seat/context minimums apply monthly (e.g., 100k 4k-blocks/month). There is no per-call minimum beyond the rounding quantum unless you opt into per-call routing.

Worked example (your sample patient with 3 chained calls inside a single 30-minute window):
- Calls: 18,000 + 2,000 + 12,000 = 32,000 tokens total in window.
- Metered blocks (4k): 32,000 / 4,000 = 8 blocks => billed 8 blocks.
- If you had chosen per-request metering, you'd bill: ceil(18k/4k)=5, ceil(2k/4k)=1, ceil(12k/4k)=3 => 9 blocks (inefficient for chaining).

Edge-case: streaming sessions that remain idle for >30 minutes open a new conversation window. Also, KV-cache reuse on repeated calls can reduce billable input tokens; Marissa can provide details on cache crediting.

I'll attach a compact pricing calc and a revised proposal that shows committed discount tiers.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Priya — adding a few commercial clarifications so the finance team can model with confidence.

Commercial notes:
- Committed discount tiers (example): 5% @ 500k blocks/month, 12% @ 1.5M blocks/month, 18% @ 3M+ blocks/month. We can structure a stepped rebate if you prefer smoothing.
- Conditional pilot concession: for an initial 6-month pilot (target 500k blocks/month), we can offer a one-time 20% credit on overages if you convert to an annual reserved contract within 90 days of pilot completion.
- Rounding/aggregation: as Sergio noted, we'll aggregate per 30-min window by default to avoid per-call inefficiencies. We'll add a line in the SOW clarifying that aggregation is per-account and not per-API key to avoid confusion across teams.

Request: could procurement confirm whether your network pattern is largely single long requests (18k) or more frequent chained calls? The pilot concession is most valuable if you actually run chains (we modeled cost for chains at the 30-min aggregation).

Thanks,

Hi Sanjay / Priya — thanks, and good clarifications. Two quick answers, and next steps below.

1) KV-cache credits: we surface explicit cache credits on the invoice as a negative token adjustment line item ("KV cache credit: -X tokens / -$Y"). That way finance can see raw token usage, cache credits applied, and the net billed tokens. We'll include a short example on page 2 of the term sheet.

2) Pilot concession: agreed we will produce a term sheet with explicit language. Proposed key points: 
- Trigger: pilot average >= 400k blocks/month for any rolling 60-day window within the 6-month pilot.
- Credit: 20% of overage value applied as invoice credit, capped at $50,000.
- Conversion: credit only applied if Acme signs an annual reserved contract within 90 days after the pilot end date.
- Audit: Redwood reserves the right to audit usage patterns to confirm chain behavior; audit limited to data required to validate billing metrics.

Attached: a red-lineable term sheet and a one-page invoice example (shows aggregation and KV credits). If this looks good, Vanessa and I will send a DocuSign.
